meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to work', paired with 'поработать'.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'oh', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no; there isn't', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

заниматься.gloss: to be busy with, to do

meanings.en: to be busy with, to do
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ниматься'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be busy with, to do', paired with 'заняться'.
High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'our, ours', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'вадьба'). Common feminine noun meaning 'wedding' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Watch the movie Wedding on Skype.

examples.text: Макс, зачем ты соврал про нашу будущую свадьбу?
examples.trans: Max, why did you lie about our future wedding?
Then a wedding, and then kids!

meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'ставлять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to imagine; to introduce, present', paired with 'представить'.

examples.trans: Can you believe it, they forgot it in the oven!

examples.text: Ты даже не представляешь, как я устал.
examples.trans: You can't even imagine how tired I am.

examples.text: Представляешь, в духовке забыли! Юль, выйди.
examples.trans: Can you believe it, they forgot it in the oven! Yul, step out.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'led, behaved', paired with 'повести'.

examples.text: Лидия Алексеевна, успокойтесь, пожалуйста! Вы как маленькая себя ведёте.
examples.trans: Lydia Alexeyevna, calm down, please! You're behaving like a little girl.
You're behaving like a little girl.

examples.text: Вы ведёте себя как подросток! Вы приударяете за мной.
examples.trans: You are behaving like a teenager! You are flirting with me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'oneself, myself, himself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, простите меня, пожалуйста. Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, please forgive me. I don't know myself how it happened.

examples.text: Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: I don't know myself how it happened.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'all right, OK', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'oneself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'married', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал. В Москву звал замуж!
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once. He asked me to marry him and come to Moscow!

examples.text: А в Париж вас никто замуж не звал?
examples.trans: And nobody asked you to marry him and move to Paris?

examples.text: Мариночка, умоляю тебя, выходи за меня замуж!
examples.trans: Marinochka, I beg you, marry me!

выйти.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.en: to go out, to get out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выходить'.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'bye', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'следний'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('last, final').

examples.trans: I'm asking for the last time.
I'm asking for the last time. Where is the money?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'left, departed'.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа.
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'глядеть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look, appear'.

examples.trans: On top the costume looks simply super!

examples.text: Не говорите так, вы прекрасно выглядите!
examples.trans: Do not say that, you look wonderful!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.
Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'mop' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Tie a broom to a mop!
She washed the floor with a mop.

examples.text: Когда нет в кармане денег. Привяжи ты к швабре веник!
examples.trans: When there is no money in your pocket. Tie a broom to a mop!

meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'some, some kind of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'such, like this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'транный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strange, odd').
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'whether, if; (что ли) or what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I don't know whether he is at home.
Was it Osipenko who hired you?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'просить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to ask (for), to request', paired with 'просить'.

examples.trans: I wanted to ask you something.
Arkash, I wanted to ask you something.
